files.landing-page.md:
# Know which invoice lines match — and which need a question.

## Purchasing paperwork operator

Turn normalized supplier invoices and purchase orders into a line-by-line reconciliation your team can review. Keep the original source close to every result.

### Start with the records you already have

Import vendor aliases, purchase orders and invoices as normalized CSV files. The operator matches vendors and exact PO lines, then compares currency, SKU, quantity and unit price using decimal arithmetic. [matching]

### Separate clean lines from unresolved questions

Review a reconciliation for every invoice line. Export clean rows as a review-ready accounting CSV, and use editable, unsent follow-up drafts to work through discrepancies. Unknown or ambiguous vendors remain review items rather than guessed matches. [outputs, traceability]

### Keep a path back to the original

Results carry the source path, SHA-256 and line reference. When a quantity or price needs a conversation, your team can find the record behind it. [traceability]

## A practical first run

Prepare the three CSV inputs, run the operator and review the reconciliation, clean-row export and exception drafts. Begin with a representative set of records and keep your existing approval process. [matching, outputs]

**Next step:** Ask us for an example reconciliation, or bring your normalized CSV layout to a setup conversation. Pricing and service scope are agreed separately; this page does not establish a paid plan.

### What stays with your team

This is not an OCR service or an automatic accounting integration. It does not send supplier messages, approve discrepancies, purchase goods or move money. The CSV export remains review-ready, not posted. [limits]
